takeaway: Clear-cell carcinoma is 75–80% of renal cell carcinoma and is driven by VHL loss. Many are found incidentally. Masses under 4 cm treated by partial nephrectomy have cancer-specific survival above 94% at five years. Metastatic combinations of immunotherapy, with or without a tyrosine-kinase inhibitor, produce responses of 42–71% [1].
clinicalQuestion: How is localised renal cell carcinoma treated, and what do modern metastatic combinations achieve?
setting: Diagnosis and treatment of renal cell carcinoma.
population: Patients with localised or metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
intervention: Partial nephrectomy for small masses; immune checkpoint combinations for advanced disease.
comparator: Active surveillance or ablation for selected small masses.
primaryOutcome: Cancer-specific survival for small tumours and response and survival for metastatic disease.
mainFindings: Clear-cell disease is 75–80% and is characterised by inactivation of VHL. Between 37% and 61% are diagnosed incidentally. Management of small masses can include ablation, radiation, or active surveillance, especially under 2 cm. For masses under 4 cm, partial nephrectomy can give a five-year cancer-specific survival above 94%. For advanced or metastatic disease, immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations, or those inhibitors plus tyrosine-kinase inhibitors, are associated with tumour response of 42–71% and median overall survival of 46–56 months. Tyrosine-kinase inhibitors block VEGF-receptor signalling. Checkpoint antibodies block PD-1 on T cells from binding PD-L1 or PD-L2 on the tumour [1].
clinicalMeaning: A small incidental mass is not an automatic radical nephrectomy. Metastatic treatment is now an immunotherapy combination, not cytokine therapy [1].
limitations: The response range pools combinations. It is not one drug's label [1].
bottomLine: VHL and clear-cell histology, partial nephrectomy for the small mass, and checkpoint combinations for metastases [1].
practiceImplication: Offer surveillance a hearing when the mass is under 2 cm [1].
trustRationale: Current JAMA review summarising ranges rather than one trial.
whatNotToOverclaim: Do not assign the 46–56 month survival to a named regimen this review pools.
